title: Routing a ship with and against the currents
query: A ship that makes 12 knots through the water sails regularly between a point off the coast at 27 S and a point off south-eastern Tasmania at 43 S, in both directions. Using the supplied GLORYS12 monthly near-surface velocity for 2011-2020 in the western Tasman Sea off south-eastern Australia (46-26 S, 147-162 E), determine how much time the currents add or save on each passage compared with still water, how much a route chosen with knowledge of the currents could gain over the shortest route, how these numbers vary by season and from year to year, and how reliable such planning would be when only monthly means are known. State the assumptions you make about the ship and the route.

region.name: Tasman Sea and East Australian Current
